observation.stability: root-caused 2026-09-22: the recorded per-application DEBUG stream depends on the oracle process's early heap allocation sequence, and pointer-keyed iteration order inside the oracle flips with it. Two levers demonstrated on next_url: (a) argv path form - relative spec/binary argv reproduces the pinned variant (records=1019, sha256=b227ae94...) while absolute argv yields a second, equally deterministic variant (records=1014, sha256=94047fd6...); (b) ASLR - with randomization on, larger functions (curl main) produce a different stream almost every run (4744/4745/4762/4763 records across four same-input runs). Environment size is irrelevant (env -i plus a 24-byte padding var reproduces the same hash). The historical '~15-minute divergent window' (records=1014, final_return=1285) was this argv/ASLR sensitivity, not a random native execution. Canonical capture recipe pinned for every function (runner determinism note): cwd=repo_root, relative argv sleigh_specs examples/<corpus>, env -i + STAGE_DRILL_FUNC/STAGE_DRILL_ADDR only, setarch -R. Under it next_url reproduces b227ae94... byte-identically (preserving the historical pin) and each functions-map target is byte-stable across repeated runs. Any future drift fails the runner's per-function sha256 pin; drift artifacts are preserved under /dev/shm/rugra-tests/sb-drill/drift/
